chapter: Instruments, tenors and the current band
title: Recording soprano in 1967 and mutual respect with Coltrane
summary: Herman first recorded soprano on Bill Holman's suite in 1967 and explains Coltrane's respect for him and how he uses soprano for excitement.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Now, I recall that it was 1967 that you first recorded the soprano, at least with the Herd on that -- what was it, "The Horn of the Fish" or that --
-- Bill Holman did for the band. Yeah, that's the suite. (unintelligible)

Right, and that actually has some, I think, some significance to the development of the use of the soprano saxophone in a wider way of the last ten years or more, because it predated, say, Wayne Shorter's entry.

Yeah, well, I think that it was one of the first people to really want to take a shot at it, like, the people of my ilk, at least. And when I heard John do it, -- and John and I had some very meaningful talks on occasion, that never lasted very long. But he could never understand why I did what I did, and I guess I stated the same case as far as he was concerned. I said that we had complete recognition and complete understanding and complete belief in

And that's -- and I just said a lot. And consequently, we had a great deal of admiration and respect for each other. And it seemed to me it would be best if I tried it. It was almost sort of a different kind of challenge. I didn't want to prove anything, not at all. I knew I never could play like John or anyone else played it. But maybe I could do some noises on soprano that somebody else hadn't done. And, after all, that's been my way of life.
Right, right. And since then, you use it rather frequently.

I've used it a lot, depending on the writer's thoughts about it and what we were trying to do and what we were trying to assume. At first, I was quite serious with it and I would knock my brains out trying to do a sensible musical thing, Body and Soul or whatever the other piece was. And then finally I thought I was really wasting my efforts because the best cup of tea with this instrument is to add they had more excitement to what the sound is with the band, whatever you're playing.
